prompt: The increase in the production of consumer goods results in damage to the natural environment. What are the causes of this? What can be done to solve this problem?
essay:
In this day and age, the increase in consumer goods production has become a major concern because it can cause serious damage to the natural environment. This problem is mainly caused by companies' efforts to control their budget. To solve this problem, some effective measures can be implemented to reduce the negative impacts of these activities.

The main reason why the increasing production of goods can damage our habitat is that many businesses do not implement effective waste handling procedures since they want to reduce their expense. As a result, untreated industrial waste is being dumped directly into nearby areas, causing serious pollution problems, namely water pollution.  For example, in 2018, Formosa company discharged a huge amount of toxic chemical substances into the ocean and destroyed the marine ecosystem in the Central region of Vietnam. This situation not only has negative impacts on marine creatures but also on the surrounding villages

There are solutions that can be taken to tackle these problems, such as issuing new policies relating to environmental problems. Most notably, governments should impose heavy fines on companies that illegally discharge unprocessed toxic chemical substances into the environment. This would encourage manufacturers to comply with environmental regulations and invest in handling their harmful byproducts.

In conclusion, the rise of consumer goods production can have negative effects on the natural habitat because companies may prioritise cost reduction over environmental protection. In order to remedy the situation, governments should apply strict penalties to factories that harm the natural habitat, thus reducing the impact on the environment.
